title: Sporting Chaos
blurb: Olympic mishaps, weird rules and sporting oddities that really happened.

prompts.text: Tug of war was an official Olympic medal event until the year _____.
The winner of the chaotic 1904 Olympic marathon, Thomas Hicks, was kept going by his trainers with brandy and the poison _____.
At the 1900 Paris Olympics there was no pool, so the swimming races were held in the River _____.
Eddie "the Eagle" Edwards, who finished last in ski jumping at the 1988 Winter Olympics, was a _____ by trade.
The 2010 Wimbledon match between John Isner and Nicolas Mahut took three days, and its fifth set ended 70 games to _____.
When James Naismith invented basketball in 1891, the first hoops were _____ baskets nailed to a gym balcony.
Don Bradman was out for a duck in his final Test innings, leaving him with a career Test batting average of _____.
The first men's football World Cup, in 1930, was both hosted and won by _____.
The only national team to have played at every men's football World Cup is _____.
Michael Phelps retired as the most decorated Olympian ever, with _____ Olympic gold medals.
Astronaut Alan Shepard hit golf balls on the Moon in 1971 with a makeshift club built around a _____ iron head.
The 1908 London Olympic marathon started at _____ Castle and finished in front of the royal box, which gave the race its odd 26.2 mile length.
Rugby union is named after a famous boarding school in the English town of Rugby, in the county of _____.
In 1962 Wilt Chamberlain scored a record _____ points in a single NBA game.
Referee boss Ken Aston came up with football's red and yellow cards in 1966 while stopped at a _____.
The Olympic torch relay from Greece was introduced at the 1936 Games in _____.
Curling stones are traditionally made from granite quarried on the Scottish island of _____.
Spyridon Louis, the Greek winner of the first modern Olympic marathon in 1896, made his living as a _____ carrier.
The Ashes got their name from a mock obituary for English cricket, printed after England lost to Australia at The _____ in 1882.
In 1966 the stolen World Cup trophy was found wrapped in newspaper by a dog called _____.
Japanese runner Shizo Kanakuri vanished during the 1912 Stockholm Olympic marathon and officially finished the race in the year _____.
When Nadia Comaneci scored the first perfect 10 in Olympic gymnastics, the scoreboard could only show _____ because it had no room for the extra digit.
Muhammad Ali and George Foreman fought the "Rumble in the Jungle" in 1974 in the country then called _____.
A maximum break in snooker, potting all 15 reds with blacks and then every colour, is worth _____ points.
The highest possible checkout in darts with three darts is _____.
At the Cooper's Hill cheese-rolling race in England, competitors chase a round of Double _____ down a steep hill.
Skateboarding made its Olympic debut at the Games delayed to 2021 and held in _____.
The Olympic motto in Latin, Citius, Altius, Fortius, means Faster, Higher, _____.
The first woman to win an individual Olympic title, in tennis at the 1900 Paris Games, was Britain's Charlotte _____.
The backwards high jump style that won gold at the 1968 Mexico City Olympics is named the _____ Flop.
At the 1936 Berlin Olympics, American sprinter Jesse Owens won _____ gold medals.
Ethiopia's Abebe Bikila won the 1960 Olympic marathon in Rome running without any _____.
Boston's long World Series drought after selling Babe Ruth to the Yankees was blamed on the Curse of the _____.
The first ever Super Bowl, in January 1967, was won by the Green Bay _____.
The NHL retired the number _____ across the whole league in honour of Wayne Gretzky.
The first race of the Formula One World Championship, in 1950, was held at the British circuit of _____.
In 1980 the US ice hockey team pulled off the "Miracle on Ice" at Lake Placid by beating the heavily favoured _____.
The Rugby World Cup trophy is named after William Webb _____, the schoolboy said to have invented the game.
England's controversial 1932-33 Ashes tactics, aimed at batsmen's bodies, became known as _____ bowling.
Because of Australia's quarantine laws, the equestrian events of the 1956 Melbourne Olympics were held in _____.
Swimmer Eric Moussambani of Equatorial Guinea won hearts at Sydney 2000 and was nicknamed Eric the _____.
Roger Bannister ran the first sub-four-minute mile in 1954 at the Iffley Road track in the English city of _____.
The NBA introduced a shot clock in 1954 to stop stalling, and it was set at _____ seconds.
